articles.summary: Regional Container Lines (RCL) will introduce an Advance Filing Surcharge as part of its compliance with the United Arab Emirates’ Maritime Preload Cargo Information (MPCI) programme. articles.body: Regional Container Lines (RCL) will introduce an Advance Filing Surcharge as part of its compliance with the United Arab Emirates’ Maritime Preload Cargo Information (MPCI) programme. The regulatory framework, also known as the Advance Manifest Filing requirement, requires shipping lines to submit import cargo manifest data electronically to UAE Customs before vessels depart from their last foreign port outside the country. Shipments covered by the MPCI programme The mandatory filing requirement applies to all containerised maritime cargo entering or passing through UAE ports, including: Local imports destined for clearance in the UAE Transshipment cargo discharged in the UAE for onward connection Transit and Freight Remaining on Board cargo passing through the UAE without discharge Shipping Instruction deadline Customers must submit complete and accurate Shipping Instructions or Bill of Lading drafts no later than 48 hours before the vessel’s estimated arrival at the port of loading. RCL warned that incomplete or late submissions could result in cargo being rolled or receiving a Do Not Load instruction from UAE Customs. Advance filing surcharge The new charge will apply from 16 October 2026, based on the vessel’s departure date at origin. Charge code Charge Scope Currency Amount Basis 42910 Advance Filing Surcharge Import, transshipment, transit and FROB USD 17 Per Bill of Lading RCL said the surcharge will cover the preparation, processing and electronic transmission of the required shipment information.

articles.summary: Two more tankers have been struck by unidentified projectiles in separate incidents near the Strait of Hormuz and in the northern Persian Gulf, adding to a growing series of attacks...

REUTERS/Stringer Two more tankers have been struck by unidentified projectiles in separate incidents near the Strait of Hormuz and in the northern Persian Gulf, adding to a growing series of attacks on commercial shipping as maritime security conditions across the region continue to deteriorate. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported Wednesday that a tanker was struck approximately 11 nautical miles west of Bukha, Oman, at 0145 UTC on October 21. The impact sparked a fire aboard the vessel, which has since been extinguished. The tanker is now at anchor, with all crew members reported safe and no environmental damage reported. In a separate incident, the master of another tanker reported being struck by an unknown projectile approximately 30 nautical miles southeast of Al Faw, Iraq, at 1830 UTC on October 20. UKMTO received the report after the incident occurred. All crew members were reported safe, with no damage to the vessel or environmental impact reported. Neither vessel has been publicly identified, and UKMTO did not attribute responsibility for either attack. The latest incidents come amid a sharp increase in attacks against commercial shipping, with violence increasingly extending beyond the Strait of Hormuz into the wider Persian Gulf. In its October 18 advisory , the Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) maintained its SEVERE threat assessment for the Strait of Hormuz, warning that deliberate attacks remained highly likely. The assessment followed a particularly violent period in which UKMTO recorded 12 attacks on commercial vessels during the week ending October 16, including 10 in the Strait of Hormuz, one in the Persian Gulf and one in the Gulf of Oman. JMIC reported 153 confirmed maritime security incidents across the region since March 1, a figure that predates the latest attacks. Recent incidents have also demonstrated the growing danger to vessels operating away from the strait’s main shipping lanes. On October 16, two tankers were attacked near Al Jubayl, Saudi Arabia, including one struck by a rocket-propelled grenade fired from a small boat. Another tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile, forcing its crew to evacuate. On October 18, a tug operating approximately 20 nautical miles northeast of Khor Fakkan, UAE, was struck by two projectiles. The vessel sustained damage but was able to continue its voyage, with one minor crew injury reported. JMIC subsequently raised the threat level for the wider Persian Gulf to SUBSTANTIAL , citing the expanding pattern of attacks and growing electronic navigation interference. The advisory also warned that vessels remaining stationary for extended periods, particularly those broadcasting AIS signals, could face increased targeting risks. The threat is becoming particularly concerning around major anchorages. As of October 18, JMIC counted approximately 217 vessels anchored near Fujairah and Khor Fakkan, with another 166 in waters stretching from Dubai and Jebel Ali toward Ras Al Khaimah. The latest attacks also follow renewed Iranian claims that commercial vessels have struck sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz. On October 17, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy claimed that two supertankers had struck mines in the waterway. JMIC said there was no substantiation for those claims. Although JMIC continues to warn mariners about possible mining activity in and around the strait’s traffic separation scheme, the two latest UKMTO warnings describe strikes by unidentified projectiles, not confirmed mine explosions. articles.title: Maersk reports further East Asia network recovery
articles.summary: Maersk has reported further progress in the recovery of its East Asia network following disruption caused by the region’s typhoon season. Operational conditions at East China ports have improved, while vessel waiting times have continued to decline compared with previous weeks. However, strong export demand from Asia...
articles.body: Maersk has reported further progress in the recovery of its East Asia network following disruption caused by the region’s typhoon season. Operational conditions at East China ports have improved, while vessel waiting times have continued to decline compared with previous weeks. However, strong export demand from Asia continues to place pressure on congested ports. Regional recovery remains ongoing Maersk said the direct impact of recent typhoon activity has largely subsided, although recovery across the wider regional network remains ongoing. Conditions across the port network continue to affect cargo flows and the recovery of vessel schedules. The carrier is working with ports, terminals and operational partners to maintain cargo movements and support the network’s recovery. This includes managing cargo flows, implementing operational adjustments where required and coordinating the use of available capacity and resources. Intermittent delays may continue Maersk said its East Asia network is becoming increasingly stable as recovery progresses. However, customers may continue to experience intermittent delays on certain trade lanes while conditions across the wider regional network return to normal. The carrier is contacting customers whose shipments may be affected to discuss available options and mitigation measures. Customers with time-sensitive or affected cargo have also been advised to contact their Maersk representative to review available solutions and contingency plans. Maersk said it will continue monitoring conditions and provide further updates as new information becomes available.

articles.title: Over 500 piles lay the foundation for Poland’s floating LNG terminal (Gallery)
articles.summary: Poland has hit a new milestone in its energy independence journey, completing the foundational piling for the new FSRU terminal in Gdańsk.
articles.body: Business Developments & Projects October 21, 2026 · 2 hours ago Over 500 piles lay the foundation for Poland’s floating LNG terminal (Gallery) Poland has hit a new milestone in its energy independence journey, completing the foundational piling for the new FSRU terminal in Gdańsk. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 4 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Completion of the installation of over 500 piles forming the foundation of the quay for the floating LNG terminal in Gdańsk Bay Source: Gaz-System With more than 500 massive steel piles now hammered into place on time and on budget, Poland’s gas transmission system operator (TSO), Gaz-System, has cleared a critical hurdle for the country's upcoming floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) in Gdańsk. This work lays the physical bedrock for a project designed to rewrite Poland's energy playbook, bringing the nation one step closer to welcoming its first FSRU vessel by early 2028. GAZ-SYSTEM has completed the driving of more than 500 piles forming the foundation of the jetty for the FSRU terminal in the Gulf of Gdańsk in accordance with the approved schedule, said to be completed on time and on budget as a key phase in the project to enable Poland to make inroads in launching the second liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal on the Polish coast. Miłosz Motyka , Minister for Energy, commented: “Developing LNG infrastructure directly strengthens Poland by securing its energy supply, boosting the economy, and upgrading the country’s position across Europe. The FSRU terminal in Gdańsk will increase our capacity to import natural gas from global markets and bolster Poland’s role in the regional supply system. “This project is of particular importance considering ongoing geopolitical tensions and the evolving dynamics of the energy landscape. The significance of strategic investment projects extends beyond the energy sector itself – they also provide a boost to Polish businesses, harness domestic expertise and lay the foundations for stable development conditions for industry and the economy as a whole.” Related Articles Clean Fuel With environmental decision in place, GAZ-SYSTEM set to proceed with Gdańsk FSRU project 3 min read The installed piles form the basis of the jetty structure and will support the platforms and enable the installation of all the equipment and systems necessary to operate the FSRUs. The construction of the offshore section of the project involves the consortium of companies, including FABE Polska . Wojciech Wrochna , Secretary of State at the Ministry of Energy and the Government Plenipotentiary for Strategic Energy Infrastructure, said: “ The completion of pile driving operation for the jetty in the FSRU Terminal in Gdańsk marks another step towards the commissioning of a new gas supply facility in Poland. “This initiative will effectively increase our gas import capacity by sea, reinforce supply diversification, and create additional opportunities for adaptable response to domestic energy demand. We remain committed to delivering investment projects that enhance the resilience and competitiveness of the Polish economy, thereby reinforcing our energy independence .” In parallel with the jetty construction, Gaz-System underlines that operations continue to integrate the offshore and onshore parts of the facility, with August 2026 marking the drilling of a microtunnel over a kilometer in length, routed under the forest, dunes, and beach in Górki Zachodnie. We faced difficult conditions and changeable weather conditions. “Nevertheless, owing to the determination of the contractors and meticulous coordination of the works, we have reached this critical milestone within the planned timeline. Now, the terminal features a robust physical foundation. Next, we will be assembling the platforms and preparing for the construction of the subsea gas pipeline .” A specialized tunnel boring machine (TBM) remained beneath the Baltic Sea seabed following the drilling operation, as it was used for the construction; thus, preparations are now in progress to facilitate its retrieval. A gas pipeline will be laid inside the tunnel connecting the terminal to the onshore part of the facility. The work on the onshore section is also well advanced, as the Gdańsk–Gustorzyn gas pipeline underwent tests in September, which is reported to have confirmed a high standard of work and the pipeline’s good working order. Łukasz Radomski , Deputy Contract Director at GAP–FABE–UNITEK Consortium, underscored: “ The steel piles driven into the seabed of the Gulf of Gdańsk form the foundation of the structure on which the prefabricated jetty platforms will be mounted along with necessary equipment. Concurrently, a microtunnel spanning over one kilometer was completed, designed for the installation of the gas pipeline connecting the offshore facility to the onshore system. “The greatest challenge was the seamless coordination of all operation components in one place and at one time; the delivery of materials, the availability of vessels and specialist equipment, and the work of teams at sea and on land. It was precisely this highly efficient logistical framework that enabled us to incorporate engineering solutions into timely project delivery.” Meanwhile, works are underway to complete the outfitting of the FSRU at the South Korean shipyard in Ulsan, with commissioning scheduled for early 2028. Following the regasification process, natural gas from the Solidarity vessel will be delivered to customers. articles.title: Port of Corpus Christi sets nine-month cargo record in 2026
articles.summary: The Port of Corpus Christi recorded its highest cargo throughput for the first nine months of 2026, handling 162.7 million tons of commodities through the Corpus Christi Ship Channel. The total represents a 6.1% increase from the previous record of 153.3 million tons, set during the same period in 2025. During the...
articles.body: The Port of Corpus Christi recorded its highest cargo throughput for the first nine months of 2026, handling 162.7 million tons of commodities through the Corpus Christi Ship Channel. The total represents a 6.1% increase from the previous record of 153.3 million tons, set during the same period in 2025. During the third quarter, port customers handled 52.4 million tons, up 3% from 50.9 million tons a year earlier. However, volumes remained below the third-quarter record of 53 million tons recorded in 2024. LNG and dry bulk drive growth Liquefied natural gas (LNG) recorded the strongest growth among the major cargo categories during the third quarter. LNG volumes increased by 46.2% to 6.6 million tons, while natural gas liquids (NGL) rose by 23.7% to 525,761 tons. Dry bulk throughput also increased, climbing 20.9% to 2.1 million tons compared with the third quarter of 2025. Meanwhile, refined petroleum products grew by 3.7% to 8.5 million tons, and other bulk liquids increased by 7.8% to 4.1 million tons. Despite these gains, several cargo categories recorded lower volumes. Crude oil shipments declined by 2.8% to 30.4 million tons, although they remained the largest cargo category handled during the quarter. Breakbulk cargo fell sharply by 94.7% to 17,041 tons. Agricultural commodities also decreased by 69% to 192,533 tons. Overall, the port’s nine-month record reflects higher cargo volumes during 2026, supported by strong growth in LNG and several bulk commodity categories.

articles.title: The Whiskey Project Group Opens North Carolina Manufacturing Facility
articles.summary: The Whiskey Project Group (TWPG) has officially opened its watercraft manufacturing facility in Edenton, North Carolina, marking a milestone in the company’s U.S. expansion and strengthening domestic production and sustainment capacity for American defense…
articles.body: The Whiskey Project Group Opens North Carolina Manufacturing Facility Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 21, 2026 © The Whiskey Project Group The Whiskey Project Group (TWPG) has officially opened its watercraft manufacturing facility in Edenton, North Carolina, marking a milestone in the company’s U.S. expansion and strengthening domestic production and sustainment capacity for American defense, government and commercial customers. The facility was officially opened at a ceremony attended by North Carolina Governor Josh Stein and Congressman Don Davis, local government representatives, defense and industry leaders, and TWPG employees and partners. Located on a 50-acre waterfront site, the 60,000 sq ft facility will serve as TWPG’s primary U.S. manufacturing and sustainment hub, supporting advanced aluminum and composite watercraft production engineering, maintenance and technical services. The facility is expected to support over 200 high-value American jobs as operations grow, with a planned investment of $10M to establish and develop its US operations. The Edenton facility establishes a key part of TWPG's dual-hub manufacturing model, connecting its U.S. operations with established design, engineering, manufacturing and sustainment capability in Yamba, Newcastle, Australia and Picton New Zealand. This integrated model provides additional production capacity and technical expertise across the Pacific, while enabling vessels to be manufactured, maintained, and supported closer to U.S. customers. It also positions TWPG to better support bilateral defense operations and long-term sustainment requirements across both countries. TWPG has secured a $36 million production contract to deliver tactical watercraft, with deliveries scheduled through September 2029. The next Whiskey vessels will be manufactured in Edenton, NC, supported by engineering, design and program expertise from TWPG Australia and its industry partners. TWPG was also selected as one of eight manufacturers for the U.S. Navy's decade-long program covering up to 474 composite rigid-hulled inflatable boats (RHIBs), with a total potential program value of up to US$650 million across all participating manufacturers if all options are exercised. The Edenton facility will support the manufacture and sustainment of TWPG's Whiskey, NAiAD and VYCOR watercraft products, with plans to progressively expand production capacity and manufacture larger vessels as U.S. operations grow.

articles.title: Shanghai and Melbourne advance green shipping corridor plans
articles.summary: The ports of Shanghai and Melbourne have launched a new implementation plan for their Green Shipping Corridor, alongside C40 Cities. Announced on October 21, 2026, the plan sets out steps to reduce emissions from container shipping between China and Australia. The two ports established the corridor in October 2025....
articles.body: The ports of Shanghai and Melbourne have launched a new implementation plan for their Green Shipping Corridor, alongside C40 Cities. Announced on October 21, 2026, the plan sets out steps to reduce emissions from container shipping between China and Australia. The two ports established the corridor in October 2025. The latest announcement moves the project from planning towards implementation. The initiative focuses on cleaner marine fuels, shore power and improved digital systems. Low-carbon container ships targeted by 2035 The partners aim to deploy at least one container ship using low-carbon fuels on the Shanghai–Melbourne route by 2035. Before deployment, they will complete studies to assess the project’s feasibility. The Port of Shanghai aims to reach an annual bunkering capacity of one million tonnes for green methanol and biofuels. The Port of Melbourne will also study the feasibility of alternative fuel bunkering. It will assess opportunities to develop shore power infrastructure. These measures aim to reduce emissions from vessels and port operations. The plan also includes digital improvements. The partners will explore better data sharing between ports and ships, alongside systems to improve voyage planning and operational efficiency. COSCO Shipping Lines joins industry collaboration Several shipping and energy companies are supporting the initiative. These include COSCO Shipping Lines, Shanghai International Port Group, HAMR Energy, ABEL Energy and Shenergy. Their work will focus on developing cleaner fuel production and supply chains. C40 Cities will coordinate activities between the ports and other partners. Saul Cannon, Chief Executive Officer of the Port of Melbourne, said the plan would help advance shore power, alternative fuel bunkering and the use of lower-emission vessels. The announcement also coincides with the 20th anniversary of the sister-port partnership between Shanghai and Melbourne. China is Melbourne’s largest trading partner. It accounts for 50% of the port’s container imports and 20% of its exports. The partners hope the corridor will provide a model for cleaner shipping on other routes between Australia and Asia.

articles.body: Business Developments & Projects October 21, 2026 · 4 hours ago Australian gas project enters home stretch as developments in Mexico and US Gulf make new inroads Woodside’s Scarborough, Trion, and Louisiana LNG projects have hit new milestones, with the finish line in sight for the first one. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 3 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Delivery of Pluto LNG module for Scarborough gas project Source: Woodside While navigating complex supply chains to deliver its projects in line with established timelines, Australia’s energy giant Woodside has advanced three major projects spanning the waters offshore Western Australia, where the almost complete Scarborough mega-project is rushing toward its first liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipment, along with deepwater milestones in Mexico and resilient construction in the U.S. Gulf. Woodside has provided updates on the progress made in developing three projects, including Scarborough offshore Australia, Trion in Mexican waters, and Louisiana LNG in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico (Gulf of America). The Scarborough and Pluto Train 2 projects remain on budget and were 99% complete at the end of the third quarter of 2026, excluding Pluto Train 1 modifications. The floating production unit (FPU) and subsea production system commissioning and start-up activities continued, including well clean-up and export of gas to pressurise the trunkline. The operator emphasizes that well clean-up results are in line with reservoir and well performance expectations. The company completed all mechanical runs of Pluto Train 2 compressors, and, subsequent to the period, Scarborough gas was introduced to the warm end (gas pre-treatment) of the LNG train. Activities in the cold end continue to progress, which will enable the start of gas liquefaction. Following the Pluto Train 1 planned major maintenance campaign in Q2, modifications to Pluto Train 1, which will allow processing of Scarborough gas, continued. The final module arrived on-site with activities focused on module hook-up and integration. The first LNG cargo is on track for Q4 2026. Liz Westcott , Woodside’s CEO, commented: “Amid ongoing volatility in global energy markets, we have remained a reliable supplier to our customers. Increased quarterly operating revenue reflected increased production and strong realized prices. “We delivered quarterly production of 46.2 million barrels of oil equivalent, up 12% from the previous quarter following the successful completion of the Pluto LNG turnaround in the second quarter and the NWS turnaround in the third quarter.” Related Articles Clean Fuel Mega $12.5 billion gas project makes inroads as FPU ends its miles-long journey in Australia 3 min read Woodside highlights that the Trion project remains on budget and was 71% complete at the end of the third quarter, as the drilling campaign moved forward, with 10 of 24 wells drilled and the first subsea tree installed. The subsea equipment and disconnectable turret mooring (DTM) buoy were delivered to Mexico, enabling offshore installation to begin. The FPU fabrication reached 96% completion, with integration and pre-commissioning activities underway. The operator progressed floating storage and offloading vessel construction, including completion of DTM turret integration into the hull. This project is targeting first oil in 2028. Related Articles Fossil Energy $10.4B oil project nears offshore installation as key equipment reaches Mexico 2 min read The Louisiana LNG project remains on budget and was 32% complete at the end of the quarter, as LNG terminal construction advanced across marine, site works, and LNG tanks, with LNG Tank 1 wall concrete reaching 50% completion. Currently, ongoing engagement with high-quality counterparties for equity participation and LNG offtake continues. The project is targeting the first LNG in 2029. The Australian energy giant claims that structural steel supply challenges associated with ongoing disruptions in the Middle East continue to be mitigated through alternative logistics routes and fabrication sources. articles.body: Dongwon Global Terminal Busan plans to expand its automated container-handling infrastructure at Busan New Port under an investment agreement signed with regional authorities. The company signed the Memorandum of Understanding with the Busan-Jinhae Free Economic Zone Authority, South Gyeongsang Province and Changwon City during an investment event held in Seoul on 20 October 2026. Under the agreement, Dongwon Global Terminal Busan plans to invest approximately KRW200 billion by 2028 in the West Container Terminal area of Busan New Port. Automated equipment and operating systems The investment will cover additional automated guided vehicles, container-handling equipment and advanced terminal operating systems. Dongwon Global Terminal Busan expects the expansion to strengthen the smart port capabilities of Busan New Port and create 88 new jobs. The Dongwon Group subsidiary opened South Korea’s first fully automated container terminal at Busan New Port in April 2024. The terminal uses automated guided vehicles, automated container cranes and an integrated operating system to handle the unloading, transportation and storage of containers. It has also introduced electrically powered equipment to improve operating efficiency and reduce the environmental impact of its operations. Wider investment agreement The agreement also includes a separate investment by medical supplies manufacturer Young Chemical. Young Chemical plans to invest KRW100 billion by 2029 in a new medical supplies and cosmetics manufacturing facility in the second phase of the Ungdong hinterland area in Jinhae-gu, Changwon. The facility will occupy approximately 33,000 square metres and is expected to create 60 jobs. Together, the two companies plan to invest KRW300 billion and create 148 jobs within the Busan-Jinhae Free Economic Zone. The Busan-Jinhae Free Economic Zone Authority said it would work with South Gyeongsang Province and Changwon City to support the necessary administrative and permitting procedures.

articles.title: First Commercial Ship-to-Ship Green Ammonia Bunkered in China
articles.summary: The FKAB-designed L21 ammonia carrier Shenghang Yongle has successfully supplied 1,000 tonnes of green ammonia to the ammonia-powered bulk carrier Mineral Europa in Zhoushan, China. A liquefied gas carrier originally designed by FKAB Marine…
articles.body: First Commercial Ship-to-Ship Green Ammonia Bunkered in China Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 21, 2026 Photo credit to Andefu Energy Technology Co., Ltd The FKAB-designed L21 ammonia carrier Shenghang Yongle has successfully supplied 1,000 tonnes of green ammonia to the ammonia-powered bulk carrier Mineral Europa in Zhoushan, China. A liquefied gas carrier originally designed by FKAB Marine Design has completed what Jiangsu Andefu Energy Development describes as the world’s first commercial ship-to-ship bunkering operation using green ammonia. On 13 October 2026, Shenghang Yongle supplied 1,000 tonnes of green ammonia to Mineral Europa, an ammonia-powered vessel owned by Belgian maritime group CMB.TECH , at the Zhoushan anchorage in Zhejiang Province, China. The operation demonstrates that green ammonia can be transferred safely from one vessel to another for use as marine fuel. FKAB developed the original L21 vessel design as a flexible semi-refrigerated and semi-pressurised liquefied gas carrier. When the vessel was selected for conversion into an ammonia bunker vessel, FKAB continued its involvement by preparing the technical drawing documentation together with cargo-handling specialist Gloryholder. “The completed bunkering operation is an important proof point for ammonia as a marine fuel. It shows how a flexible vessel platform, supported by the right engineering and safety systems, can become part of the infrastructure needed for shipping’s transition away from fossil fuels. We are proud that an FKAB-designed vessel has helped bring commercial ship-to-ship green ammonia bunkering into operational reality,” says Peter Hermansson, Managing Director of FKAB Marine Design. Jiangsu Andefu Energy Development led the conversion and certification process in close cooperation with China Classification Society . FKAB and Gloryholder prepared the technical drawing documentation required for the conversion. The conversion included modifications to the bunkering system, development of operating procedures, risk assessments, and the establishment of safety and emergency-response arrangements. Particular attention was given to ammonia toxicity, material compatibility, low-temperature operation, leak detection and risk control during bunkering. Shenghang Yongle completed its conversion in August 2026 and received the first class certificate for liquid ammonia bunkering issued by a classification society. The bunkering operation in Zhoushan has now demonstrated the vessel’s capability in practice.

articles.body: OEG Orders Three More Offshore Wind CTVs from Diverse Marine Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 21, 2026 (Credit: Diverse Marine) OEG Marine Services has ordered three additional crew transfer vessels (CTVs) from Diverse Marine, expanding its offshore wind support fleet under a newbuilding program scheduled for delivery throughout 2027. The vessels will be built to the BREVITY SL Class design developed by Chartwell Marine, with each measuring 26 metres in overall length and having a load line length of less than 24 metres. All three CTVs will be constructed to the same specification, classed by Bureau Veritas and operated under the UK flag. The vessels will feature quad Volvo Penta IPS propulsion compliant with IMO Tier III emissions standards, alongside Hull Vane transom foils designed to improve fuel efficiency at cruising speeds. The contract marks the second collaboration between OEG and Diverse Marine, following the delivery of the OEG Fulmar in 2025. The three new vessels will support OEG's fleet renewal and expansion programme, with the company planning to deploy them in offshore wind operations from 2027. "This contract marks the second collaboration for OEG with Diverse Marine, and we are pleased to continue working together to progress our fleet renewal and expansion program. "The Chartwell design has proved to perform above expectations, and the quality of the build from Diverse bears testament to us continuing the relationship for a further three vessels. "These new vessels will help OEG to continue to provide the best service to our clients for 2027 and beyond," said Leif Cooper, Director of OEG Marine Services. Diverse Marine will build the vessels at its facilities in Cowes, continuing its collaboration with Chartwell Marine on the BREVITY design. The order follows the companies' previous work on OEG Fulmar and adds three larger vessels to OEG's fleet.

articles.body: Hateco Group and APM Terminals have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to study the investment, development and operation of railway freight terminals in Vietnam. The agreement was signed on 20 October 2026 in Denmark during the Vietnam–Denmark Business Forum. The ceremony took place during the State visit of General Secretary and President To Lam and was witnessed by senior representatives from both countries. APM Terminals is part of A.P. Moller – Maersk. The non-binding agreement expands the cooperation between Hateco and APM Terminals from container port infrastructure to railway connectivity and multimodal logistics. Railway freight terminal planned in Hai Phong Under the MOU, the companies will jointly study and propose the development and operation of a railway freight terminal in Hai Phong. The proposed facility would include a cargo-handling centre and storage yards. Hateco and APM Terminals will also examine three additional railway freight locations in northern Vietnam. The proposed network would connect industrial parks, manufacturing centres and logistics hubs with the country’s seaports. The facilities are expected to use digital technology for cargo reception, management, storage and transshipment. If developed, the network would support container movements between northern Vietnam’s industrial areas, Hai Phong’s port system and international shipping routes. The parties expect the proposed connections to improve transport efficiency, reduce pressure on road infrastructure and support Vietnam’s import and export supply chains. Cooperation extends beyond port infrastructure The railway initiative follows the cooperation between Hateco and APM Terminals at Hateco Hai Phong International Container Terminal in the Lach Huyen port area. HHIT began operations in April 2025 and can accommodate container vessels with capacities of up to 18,000 TEUs. Hateco and APM Terminals are also pursuing cooperation on other port and logistics infrastructure projects in Vietnam. The wider planned investments involving Hateco and Maersk in Vietnam are estimated at between US$2.5 billion and US$3.5 billion. This amount does not represent the investment value of the railway freight terminal project alone.

articles.body: Uncategorized AG Seville wins 25-year port shipyard concession with $11m investment plan Splash Ports October 21, 2026 0 67 1 minute read AG Seville Shipyard AG Seville Shipyard AG Seville Shipyard has won the competition to continue operating the ship repair facilities at Spain’s Port of Seville, clearing an important hurdle for a proposed €10m ($11.2m) investment programme. Seville Port Authority’s board approved the selection of AG Seville Shipyard on October 20, allowing the company to retain its position at the former Astilleros del Guadalquivir facilities. The operator’s existing concession expires in December.The new concession will cover approximately 22,000 sq m of port land and infrastructure, including the dry dock, the southern section of the Muelle de Armamento and a disused slipway. The concession can run for up to 25 years, although final administrative approval is still required before the new agreement becomes effective. AG Seville Shipyard faced competition for the facilities from Spanish maritime group Boluda, which had also expressed interest in taking over the site. The successful operator has controlled part of the former Seville shipyard since 2017, developing ship repair and maintenance operations at facilities that had suffered years of decline following the collapse of the former public shipyard. The company plans to invest approximately €10m ($11.2m) in modernisation and expansion projects under the new concession. The tender conditions also require the successful operator to invest at least €3m ($3.4m) during the first three years, including improvements to the slipway and dry dock infrastructure. The larger €10m programme is AG Seville’s proposed investment plan, rather than an amount separately confirmed as contractually committed in the latest announcement. The port authority also approved an additional €4.2m ($4.7m) for improvements to Seville’s port free zone. The decision raises the total budget for modernising the area to €8m ($9m), covering electrical infrastructure, roads, lighting and other facilities serving businesses operating within the port’s industrial zone. The port authority will oversee procurement and technical management of the improvement projects. articles.summary: Chinese front-loading is expected to have run its course, pointing to softer bauxite flows in 2026 Q4. • Global bauxite flows increased by 2.8% y/y in September. • Flows arriving in China increased by 21.2% y/y in September • Flows arriving in the UAE fell by over 60.0% in September. • Bauxite arriving in India ...
articles.body: Signal: The final quarter of 2026 is expected to see softer bauxite flows in Dry Bulk Market , International Shipping News 21/10/2026 Chinese front-loading is expected to have run its course, pointing to softer bauxite flows in 2026 Q4. • Global bauxite flows increased by 2.8% y/y in September. • Flows arriving in China increased by 21.2% y/y in September • Flows arriving in the UAE fell by over 60.0% in September. • Bauxite arriving in India declined by 37.0% y/y in September, the largest y/y decrease of any month in 2026 so far. Bauxite flows in September 2026 rose 3% to 20.4 Mt, driven by higher flows from Guinea. Flows fell m/m, but this was expected as September falls within the wet season, which typically reduces the ability of material to flow out of the ports. Compared to September 2025, flows from Guinea increased by over 20%. China received a surge of seaborne bauxite inflows during September, reaching 19.7 Mt, up over 21% from the same period a year earlier. Disruptions to shipping norms in the Arabian Gulf have continued to affect bauxite arrivals in the UAE, and some regional processing facilities are operating below normal utilization levels, leading to a 60% drop in bauxite arrivals in September 2026. India has been a key landing spot for seaborne bauxite that could not reach the Arabian Gulf, with Q1 and Q2 arrivals well ahead of the previous year. 2026 Q3 finished with a decrease y/y of 13.8%. This was driven by several factors, such as adequate stocks not requiring additional material and monsoons affecting domestic logistics operations. The outlook for global bauxite flows is softer in Q4 2026, with Guinea’s export restrictions expected to constrain shipments in the final months of the year. In June, Guinea introduced an annual export quota of 150 Mt, 18% below 2025 levels. However, Signal Ocean data show Guinean bauxite exports up 21% year-to-date, implying that shipments will need to slow materially in Q4. Demand growth elsewhere is unlikely to offset this reduction. India remains well supplied, limiting the need for stronger year-on-year imports, while persistent regional tensions and disruption are expected to constrain demand recovery in the Arabian Gulf. Chinese demand should remain comparatively resilient, but significant upside appears limited: bauxite arrivals were flat year-on-year in Q3, suggesting little underlying growth in import requirements. With Guinea accounting for the majority of China’s imported bauxite, lower Guinean loadings are likely to translate into weaker Chinese arrivals, although existing inventories and cargoes already in transit may cushion the initial impact. Overall, the balance of risks points to softer global bauxite flows in Q4. Front loading leads to a weaker final quarter outlook Global bauxite flows are expected to soften in Q4 as Chinese front-loading eases and Guinea’s export restrictions begin to constrain supply. September’s surge in Chinese arrivals contrasts with weakening demand across India and the Arabian Gulf, where adequate stocks and ongoing regional disruption limit the potential for a recovery. With Indian inventories well supplied and Gulf processing activity subdued, neither market is likely to absorb significantly more seaborne material in the coming months. China should remain the principal destination for global bauxite, but flat year-on-year arrivals in Q3 suggest limited scope for further demand growth. Although cargoes already in transit and existing inventories may cushion the initial impact, lower Guinean loadings are likely to weigh on arrivals towards year-end. Consequently, the balance of risks points to weaker global flows and reduced Capesize tonne-mile demand in Q4. articles.body: Capital Maritime Finance: Historic Listing on Euronext Athens, with Unprecedented Participation from Retail Investors in Hellenic Shipping News 21/10/2026 Capital Maritime Finance Corp. (“CMF”) has completed the most successful public offering in recent years, with the exception of Athens International Airport (AIA), marking the first-ever exclusive listing of a shipping company on the Regulated Market of Euronext Athens, with total demand reaching a record €1.1 billion. Strong demand led to an increase in the size of the offering from €250 million to €300 million. Rather than fully exhausting its pricing flexibility, CMF chose to set the offering price of the new shares at €7.50 per share, thereby leaving upside potential for new shareholders. A total of 40,000,000 new shares were allocated, representing a significant free float of approximately 28.6%. Participation by Greek retail investors was unprecedented by public offering standards, with approximately 14,000 subscriptions, equivalent to 50% of the active domestic investment accounts on Euronext Athens. Retail investors were allocated 20,546,668 shares, representing 67% of the new shares allocated, excluding cornerstone shares, while total demand from retail investors reached 61,598,531 shares. Interest from foreign institutional portfolios and Greek institutional investors was also particularly strong. These investors were allocated 10,120,000 shares, representing 33% of the total new shares allocated, excluding cornerstone shares, while total demand from this investor category amounted to 73,808,234 shares. The public offering also attracted several of Greece’s largest business groups as cornerstone investors, specifically the Vardinogiannis, Mytilineos, Peristeris and Kokkalis groups, with a total investment of €70 million, corresponding to 9,333,332 new shares, or 23.3% of the total offering. articles.title: EU Arctic Strategy: NGOs Welcome EU Ambition on on Cutting Shipping’s Arctic Black Carbon Emissions
articles.summary: Responding to today’s publication of the EU’s Arctic Strategy, which definitively states the EU’s intention to support International Maritime Organization (IMO) regulations that would regulate the impacts of black carbon emissions from ships on the Arctic, Dr Sian Prior, Lead Advisor to the Clean Arctic Alliance...
articles.body: EU Arctic Strategy: NGOs Welcome EU Ambition on on Cutting Shipping’s Arctic Black Carbon Emissions in International Shipping News 21/10/2026 Responding to today’s publication of the EU’s Arctic Strategy, which definitively states the EU’s intention to support International Maritime Organization (IMO) regulations that would regulate the impacts of black carbon emissions from ships on the Arctic, Dr Sian Prior, Lead Advisor to the Clean Arctic Alliance said: “With a proposal for mandatory regulation for ‘polar fuels’ – currently on the table at the IMO – the EU ambition to cut black carbon from Arctic shipping comes at the perfect moment. The polar fuels proposal led by Denmark – supported by Greenland, and co-sponsored by Germany, France and the Solomon Islands, if accepted, would ensure that ships will be restricted to using cleaner fuels while sailing in Arctic waters. The EU’s call for a broad definition of Wider Arctic Waters – above 60o latitude north, encompassing the Arctic circle is not only welcome, it demonstrates a clear understanding that black carbon emissions from shipping close to Arctic waters travel further north and have a detrimental impact on land-ice and sea-ice in the region by driving further ice melt and climate warming.” “Other Arctic, and near-Arctic countries must now follow the EU’s lead by backing the proposal, which is due to be considered during the IMO’s Pollution Prevention and Response Committee in January 2027 (PPR14)”, added Prior. The text of the EU Arctic Strategy reads: “The EU champions renewable and low-carbon fuels for ships calling at EU ports, driven by the FuelEU maritime regulation and the EU Emissions Trading System. At the international level, the EU will contribute actively to negotiations at the International Maritime Organisation to facilitate the transition of Black Carbon measures from voluntary guidelines to binding regulations. The EU will advocate for the definition of wider Arctic waters (above 60°N) to ensure regulations cover the actual footprint of Arctic shipping.” “Canada should align with the clear signal sent by the EU decision to prioritise cutting of black carbon emissions from shipping”, said Andrew Dumbrille, Special Advisor to the Clean Arctic Alliance and co-director of Equal Routes. “Canada has already shown leadership by joining the COP30 black carbon pledge, and by bringing its Arctic emission control area into force. Canada’s next step should be to match the EU’s ambition by backing a mandatory polar fuel measure at the IMO that covers the full Arctic.” “Black carbon from shipping is accelerating the melt of sea ice in the Arctic region, which is warming four times faster than the rest of the planet”, added Dumbrille, “Reducing black carbon emissions protects local community food systems, the integrity of Canada’s Arctic waters, and the ability to steward them. Acting alongside the EU is also a matter of sovereignty, it means Canada is setting the standards for Arctic shipping rather than leaving their definition to others. Arctic states, led by Canada, should work with the EU to close this regulatory gap.” “With Iceland, along with Norway, already cooperating with the EU on climate policy, Iceland must support and align itself with the EU on cutting black carbon emissions from shipping in the Arctic”, said Arni Finnsson, Board Chair at the Iceland Nature Conservation Association. “As Iceland’s Parliament adopted an Arctic policy in 2022; a policy which acknowledged the dangers posed by black carbon. Iceland should support the polar fuels proposal at the International Maritime Organization.” “By leading the polar fuel proposal at the IMO, Greenland and Denmark have clearly demonstrated global climate leadership”, said Dr Kåre Press-Kristensen, senior advisor on air quality & climate at Green Global Future. This leadership is now reflected in the EU Arctic Strategy which thereby significantly increases the pressure for the IMO to reduce black carbon emissions from Arctic shipping. Hopefully, the EU Arctic Strategy will, as well, generate full support for the polar fuel proposal from other Arctic states like Iceland, Canada and Norway.” “Bellona welcomes the EU Arctic Strategy’s clear position on reducing harmful black carbon emissions from shipping in the Arctic”, said Sigurd Enge, Senior Advisor, Shipping and Arctic issues at Bellona. “This should be a requirement for ships who arrive from arctic waters and a clear message to the Russian government and their ambition for shipping on the Northern Sea Route. The EU Arctic strategy’s weakened signal to not purchase Norway’s oil & gas from the arctic is on the contrary not helpful in reducing the environmental impact of the vulnerable eco systems.” “WWF welcomes the clear commitment in the new EU Arctic Strategy to tackle black carbon emissions from ships in the region which has been affected by them the most”, said Karoline Andaur, CEO of WWF-Norway. “We call on Arctic governments, including the government of Norway, to support the adoption of mandatory regulations over black carbon emissions during the forthcoming meeting of the International Maritime Organization in January 2027. This will be consistent with the general commitment of Norway and its European neighbours and allies to reduce the impact from shipping on climate, ecosystems and human health.” Polar Fuels A polar fuel regulation as currently proposed by Denmark, Germany, France and the Solomon Islands would fill an important gap in the IMO’s current regulatory framework, by directly targeting black carbon emissions from ships. This polar fuel measure would require the use of cleaner distillate fuels such as marine gas oil (MGO) and new zero carbon fuels which are beginning to enter the market. It would prevent the use of residual fuel blends including marine diesel oil (MDO) and ultra-low sulphur fuel oils (ULSFOs), or heavy residual fuel oils (HFOs) with scrubbers, which would still be able to be used under an ECA designation. Source: Clean Arctic Alliance 2026-10-21 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.title: Possible further delay to road transport’s inclusion in EU ETS causes serious concern
articles.summary: Interferry, the global trade association representing the ferry shipping industry, is raising serious concerns over the current state of EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) negotiations and the persistent regulatory imbalance unfairly penalizing maritime transport. As member states push to further delay the EU ETS2...
articles.body: Possible further delay to road transport’s inclusion in EU ETS causes serious concern in International Shipping News 21/10/2026 Interferry, the global trade association representing the ferry shipping industry, is raising serious concerns over the current state of EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) negotiations and the persistent regulatory imbalance unfairly penalizing maritime transport. As member states push to further delay the EU ETS2 framework for road transport, ferry operators face an ongoing competitive disadvantage against a higher-emitting mode of transport. Since 2024, commercial passenger and cargo ships of 5,000 GT and above calling at European ports have been subject to the EU ETS, with compliance costs currently equivalent to approximately EUR 250 per tonne of diesel fuel. For European ro-pax and ro-ro ferry operators, the annual cost is estimated at approximately EUR 1 billion. While intended to incentivize a transition to cleaner fuels, this burden operates in a heavily distorted market. Ferry routes often compete directly with road transport, yet road freight, a significantly higher-emitting sector, continues to benefit from delays to its dedicated EU ETS2 framework. Already postponed from 2027 to 2028, ETS2 is facing renewed pressure from several EU member states for further delays. This possibility results from grouping road transport into the same regulatory category as the building sector. Consequently, political anxieties, particularly in Eastern and Southern European member states, over winter heating costs for households are shielding road freight from emissions trading. For ferry operators, however, the resulting market distortion is real and damaging, regardless of the political motives behind it. Higher, unevenly distributed costs resulting from the EU ETS are leading in part to a shift in transportation away from ferry services. At the same time, these disparities make it significantly more difficult to pass the additional costs to customers. Ultimately, this results in a lack of the necessary investments for the rapid decarbonization of the sector. Interferry reiterates its position: regulatory relief for one sector must not come at the expense of fair market competition, and road transport cannot continue to be exempted from genuine greenhouse gas pricing. Furthermore, Interferry insists that all revenues collected from maritime ETS compliance must be strictly ring-fenced and reinvested into decarbonizing the maritime sector itself: through EU-produced sustainable marine fuels, clean technologies, and onshore charging infrastructure. “The ETS review addresses many valid points, particularly the use of funds collected for the decarbonization of shipping. However, allowing residential heating concerns to grant an unearned commercial advantage to road freight transport over ferry shipping is unacceptable,” says Johan Roos, Director of Regulatory Affairs at Interferry, and continues: “The burdens and challenges of decarbonization cannot be borne by individual sectors alone, and all transport sectors must be treated equally. To restore fairness, EU policymakers must make the scope of ETS2 more granular by separating road transport from building emissions to ensure fair competition or, alternatively, apply carbon costs uniformly across all sectors. Anything less simply cements the existing unfair competitive disadvantage, offering no benefit to the climate or the environment.” Interferry is the global ferry trade association with consultative status at the International Maritime Organization and similar influence at the European Union as well as many other maritime governance authorities. With membership exceeding 280 companies and representing plus 2,200 individuals in more than 40 countries, its primary purposes are to represent the ferry industry on regulatory and policy matters, including safety and sustainability; to speak on behalf of the worldwide ferry sector, which provides transport for over four billion passengers and 370 million vehicles annually; and to facilitate networking and communications among its members. Source: Interferry 2026-10-21 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

For European ro-pax and ro-ro ferry operators, the annual cost is estimated at approximately EUR 1 billion.
While intended to incentivize a transition to cleaner fuels, this burden operates in a heavily distorted market.

articles.title: Transport of live animals by sea: New rules should improve safety for animals, seafarers and the environment
articles.summary: Revised rules on the transport of live animals by sea are being negotiated in the EU. Danish Shipping wants to ensure good animal welfare, seafarer safety and a level playing field for everyone transporting animals by sea in the EU. EU Member States are making progress in negotiations on new rules for the transport...
articles.body: Transport of live animals by sea: New rules should improve safety for animals, seafarers and the environment in International Shipping News 21/10/2026 Revised rules on the transport of live animals by sea are being negotiated in the EU. Danish Shipping wants to ensure good animal welfare, seafarer safety and a level playing field for everyone transporting animals by sea in the EU. EU Member States are making progress in negotiations on new rules for the transport of live animals. Danish Shipping welcomes this work but emphasises that better animal welfare must go hand in hand with higher safety standards at sea and a level playing field for EU- and non-EU-flagged ships. The aim should be to improve animal welfare, prevent accidents, ensure fair competition and help raise international standards for the transport of live animals. “Transporting live animals carries a particular responsibility. It therefore makes good sense to set high standards for both ships and their equipment. Our members already operate to high standards, and we now want these to apply much more widely across all ships transporting live animals to and from the EU. The same high safety standards must apply to all ships permitted to operate from European ports,” says Nina Porst, Executive Director of Sustainable Ships and Skills at Danish Shipping. Three years on, the European Commission’s proposal for new rules on the transport of live animals is still under consideration in the European Parliament and the Council. This will improve animal welfare and increase safety for the seafarers working on board Nina Porst, Executive Director of Sustainable Ships and Skills at Danish Shipping A 2025 study by the European Parliamentary Research Service highlights, among other things, persistent problems that may affect animal welfare. It also identifies challenges with enforcement and inspections in some Member States. Together with European Shipowners, Danish Shipping has proposed strengthening the approval requirements for ships transporting live animals. A central demand is that all ships authorised to transport live animals from the EU should meet high and comparable standards for both the vessel itself and its arrangements for carrying animals, regardless of the flag they fly. This is about both animal welfare and safety. If a ship is unsafe, animal welfare cannot be properly safeguarded either. “Put simply, we are asking for non-EU-flagged ships to undergo the same survey and approval process as EU-flagged ships. This will improve animal welfare and increase safety for the seafarers working on board. Improving ship safety also means better protection for the environment. The new rules must ensure a level playing field for all operators,” says Nina Porst. Where does the EU proposal stand? December 2023: The Commission presents a proposal for a new regulation on the protection of animals during transport. Council: Experts from EU Member States have been negotiating the text on an ongoing basis. The latest amendments are being considered by the Council’s working party on animal welfare. European Parliament: The transport and agriculture committees are jointly considering the proposal. Next steps: Once Parliament and the Council have established their negotiating positions, the two institutions and the Commission can begin trilogue negotiations on the final legislative text. This work is currently expected to begin in early 2027. Source: Danish Shipping 2026-10-21 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.title: Veson Nautical partners with Seaber to accelerate pre-fixture optimization in IMOS
articles.summary: Maritime data and technology provider Veson Nautical and scheduling and optimization company Seaber today announced a new integration to connect voyage workflows, enabling an optimized plan to become a live estimate in one step. The integration connects Veson’s flagship solution IMOS with Seaber’s scheduling and...
articles.body: Veson Nautical partners with Seaber to accelerate pre-fixture optimization in IMOS in International Shipping News 21/10/2026 Maritime data and technology provider Veson Nautical and scheduling and optimization company Seaber today announced a new integration to connect voyage workflows, enabling an optimized plan to become a live estimate in one step. The integration connects Veson’s flagship solution IMOS with Seaber’s scheduling and optimization platform, removing a manual hand-off between planning and commitment. Charterers can now build and compare fleet scenarios in Seaber and send decisions directly to IMOS, eliminating the once tedious process of sifting through disparate position lists and spreadsheets to choose vessel and cargo combinations for estimating. Charterers build and compare full fleet scenarios in Seaber’s optimization engine before the voyage details are sent to IMOS, creating and saving the estimate in one step. IMOS then builds the route and calculates freight, P&L, and time charter equivalent (TCE) data. Doing so streamlines pre-fixture and fleet optimization workflows, giving teams more time to test options with fully trusted data straight from the system of record. “An estimate tells you what one voyage is worth. A schedule tells you which voyages your fleet should run, in what order, and what the whole plan earns,” said Seaber Chief Revenue Officer Jean-Guy Faubert. “Charterers optimize that schedule in Seaber, compare the scenarios and P&L side by side, and the voyage they commit to lands in IMOS as a saved estimate. Same data, same system their team already works in, no manual re-entry.” The integration eliminates manual re-entry and shortens the time between suggesting a schedule and executing on it. IMOS, as part of the Veson Platform, remains the system of record, where estimates are refined before being handed to operations. And because scenario work happens upstream in Seaber, teams can test more options without disturbing the live voyage P&L. It’s a connection that not only streamlines pre-fixture workflows, but gives clients the flexibility to leverage the tools they rely on and the Veson Platform’s native capabilities. “By connecting Seaber’s optimization solution directly to IMOS, we’re removing a manual step that slowed teams down between planning and commitment,” said Veson Nautical VP of Strategy & Operations Matt Filosa. “This is the value the Veson Platform is built to deliver: an open platform that offers clients more capabilities from the systems they trust, without changing how they work.” Source: Veson Nautical 2026-10-21 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.summary: Maersk (Maersk) will undertake its first planned drydocking in India, with the Singapore-flagged container vessel Maersk Chattogram scheduled to enter L&T Shipbuilding’s Kattupalli Shipyard near Chennai, in October 2026. articles.body: Maersk partners with L&T for its first planned drydocking in India in Shipbuilding News 21/10/2026 Maersk (Maersk) will undertake its first planned drydocking in India, with the Singapore-flagged container vessel Maersk Chattogram scheduled to enter L&T Shipbuilding’s Kattupalli Shipyard near Chennai, in October 2026. The activity marks the first operational milestone arising from the Memorandum of Understanding signed by Maersk and Larsen & Toubro (L&T) during India Maritime Week 2025. The MoU established a framework for exploring collaboration in shipbuilding, ship repair and exchange of knowledge on global standards and building world-class capability, capacity and resources. Maersk Chattogram is expected to arrive at the shipyard on 20 October 2026, subject to operational and weather conditions. The planned drydocking forms part of the vessel’s normal lifecycle and will include its scheduled special survey, along with maintenance and overhaul work covering the hull and structure, machinery, equipment and propulsion systems. Drydocking is a planned process in which a vessel is taken into a dry dock, enabling extensive inspection, maintenance and repair areas of the vessel that are ordinarily submerged alongside work on machinery, equipment and propulsion system. It is essential to maintaining a vessel’s safety, seaworthiness, operational performance and reliability for the next five years. Maersk Chattogram will undergo a specialised lift out operation using India’s largest Shiplift system at L&T Shipbuilding, Kattupalli, to lift the vessel out of water. The drydocking of Maersk Chattogram in India is a meaningful step towards turning our collaboration with L&T into action. We are aligning Maersk’s global technical requirements with India’s growing shipyard, supplier and maritime-service capabilities. We believe India has strong potential to become an increasingly important global hub for maritime sector and we are committed to supporting that development through long-term partnerships, operational experience and knowledge sharing.” Dinesh Kumar Balraj Head of Fleet Operations East, A.P. Moller – Maersk The docking of Maersk Chattogram at Kattupalli advances our strategic partnership under the MoU and Framework Agreement signed between our organisations. Combining Maersk’s global maritime expertise with L&T’s shipbuilding capabilities, we aim to strengthen domestic capabilities and supply chains across the shipbuilding ecosystem. We share Maersk’s commitment to India’s maritime development and seek to play a key role in establishing India as a globally competitive maritime hub. Arun Ramchandani Head – Precision Engineering & Systems, L&T The project is expected to bring together Maersk’s fleet and technical teams with L&T, Indian subcontractors, suppliers and maritime service providers. The partners will focus on safe, efficient execution, quality delivery and the exchange of operational knowledge throughout the docking. The activity reinforces Maersk’s broader commitment to India’s maritime development and its belief in the country’s engineering talent, infrastructure and potential across the maritime value chain. It also reflects the long-term intent of the Maersk-L&T partnership, moving from an exploratory framework to a concrete vessel-maintenance project in India. Source: Maersk 2026-10-21 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.title: Fujairah bunker sales increased in September

Changes in Fujairah bunker fuel sales from August to September: • Total sales up by 5% to...
articles.body: Fujairah bunker sales increased in September in Port News 21/10/2026 Increased sales of HSFO and LSMGO contributed to lifting Fujairah’s total bunker sales higher in September than in August, according to data compiled by Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) and S&P Global Commodity Insights. Changes in Fujairah bunker fuel sales from August to September: • Total sales up by 5% to 231,000 mt • VLSFO sales down by 3% to 143,000 mt • HSFO sales up by 18% to 68,000 mt • LSMGO sales up by 27% to 19,000 mt Fujairah’s bunker sales increased by 5% in September, after declining in the previous month, averaging around 7,700 mt/day, up by roughly 600 mt/day from August. HSFO sales rose by around 10,000 mt to 68,000 mt in September, averaging approximately 2,300 mt/day. LSMGO sales also increased, rising by around 4,000 mt to 19,000 mt in September. In contrast, sales of VLSFO, typically the most in-demand bunker fuel grade, fell by roughly 5,000 mt during the month. Fuel grade share of total sales in September (compared to the year to date): • 62% VLSFO 380cst (62% YTD) • 0.21% VLSFO 180cst (0.29% YTD) • 29% HSFO (32% YTD) • 8% LSMGO (6% YTD) • 0.14% of 0.50% MGO (0.07% YTD) Source: By Shilpa Sharma, ENGINE, https://www.engine.online/news/ 2026-10-21 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.body: MMI Daily Iron Ore Index Report October 21 2026 in Chinese iron ore and steelmaking prices 21/10/2026 Demand showed marginal improvement, but prices did not move consistently higher. Surveyed daily hot metal output rose to 2.3584 million mt on Oct 21, up 6,400 mt, and the blast furnace operating rate increased to 87.16%. The 61%, 58% and 65% port indices each rose 1 yuan and DCE most-traded held at 681.5 yuan/mt. In contrast, the seaborne 61% and 65% indices eased to USD 90.40 and 107.40/dmt, with all 12 brands lower, reflecting different assessments of demand and resource availability across markets. Higher hot metal may increase baseline consumption, but sustained restocking still depends on raw-material stocks, finished-steel orders and mill profitability. Lower recent arrivals help ease pressure from incoming flows, while existing port stocks require actual collections for absorption. Meanwhile, higher C3 and C5 freight may alter cost conditions for some cargoes; ore prices and transport costs do not always move together. The near-term focus is whether improved production translates into persistent transactions. Buying that merely follows current consumption could leave prices range-bound, while stronger restocking and orders would provide firmer downside support. A single increase in hot metal does not establish a trend reversal; trading, production and inventories should be assessed together. articles.body: Oman’s Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology has confirmed that a new operator will take over the Port of Salalah following the expiry of the existing concession agreement. Salalah Port Services Company SAOG will continue operating the port under the current concession until its contractual expiry on 1 November 2028. The company received formal notification that the agreement will not be extended beyond that date. The notification states that the decision not to extend the concession is final and unconditional. Operations to continue until concession expiry The Ministry said port operations and development activities will continue throughout the remaining concession period. The announcement forms part of the Ministry’s commitment to maintaining operational continuity while supporting the expansion and development of the Port of Salalah. The new operator that will assume responsibility for the port after the existing concession expires will be announced in due course. Company assesses implications Salalah Port Services said its Board of Directors will review the notification and assess its implications and potential impact on the company. The company will also engage with relevant stakeholders and provide the market with updates on any material developments in accordance with applicable disclosure requirements.

The outlook was discussed during a video meeting between SCA Chairman Adm. Ossama Rabiee and senior Maersk executives, including...
articles.body: Maersk expects all its shipping services to return to the Suez Canal by March 2027, according to the Suez Canal Authority (SCA), as the carrier continues to adjust its sailing schedules. The outlook was discussed during a video meeting between SCA Chairman Adm. Ossama Rabiee and senior Maersk executives, including Chief Operating Officer Rabab Boulos. According to the SCA, Boulos expressed her expectation that all Maersk shipping services would resume transits through the canal by March next year. The timeline remains an expectation rather than a confirmed schedule for the full return of the carrier’s services. Maersk transits increase through Suez The Suez Canal Authority reported a significant increase in Maersk-affiliated vessel transits during the first nine months of 2026. articles.body: Europe Ports and Logistics Australian fund takes control of UK ports giant in £10bn deal Sam Chambers October 21, 2026 0 2,610 1 minute read Associated British Ports Associated British Ports Australian infrastructure investor IFM Investors has agreed to acquire a controlling stake in Associated British Ports (ABP), Britain’s largest port operator, in a deal valuing the business at more than £10bn ($13.4bn). The transaction will see Canadian pension giants CPP Investments and OMERS sell their combined 63.88% stake in ABP to Global Infraco Haven Bidco, an indirect subsidiary of the IFM Global Infrastructure Fund. Its activities span containers, vehicles, bulk commodities, cruise shipping and offshore energy infrastructure. The deal brings an end to two decades of Canadian involvement in the port operator. OMERS was part of the consortium that took ABP private in 2006 for £2.8bn, while CPP Investments acquired its interest in 2015. Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC and Kuwait’s Wren House Infrastructure remain among the group’s minority investors. IFM is owned by Australian and British pension funds and manages around $96bn in infrastructure assets globally. The acquisition comes as ABP pursues substantial investment across its network. As Splash reported in August, the company is advancing a £500m development at Port Talbot in Wales to establish a major floating offshore wind manufacturing and assembly hub. articles.body: Exploration & Production October 21, 2026 · 7 hours ago Norway set on tapping into Arctic gas potential: New study to unlock 1988 Barents Sea discovery Norway is targeting untapped Arctic energy by commissioning a new study to shed more light on the 1988 gas discovery in the Barents Sea. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 3 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Illustration Credit: Morten Berentsen/Norwegian Offshore Directorate Decades after being left behind in the frozen depths of the High North, a forgotten 1980s gas find in the Barents Sea is getting a second look. As Europe hungers for new energy sources and low-carbon reserves, Norway is launching a fresh push to unlock the untapped potential of the Arctic, starting with a neglected discovery 200 kilometers north of the Arctic Circle. The Barents Sea is home to a number of discoveries that could hold vast volumes of gas but remains less explored than other parts of the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS), with several discoveries in these waters potentially containing significant volumes of gas, according to the Norwegian Offshore Directorate, which emphasizes that a new study could uncover major opportunities for one of these discoveries. The gas discovery that this study will aim to gain more insight into is Norselhøgda (the well 7226/11-1 ), which is situated about 200 kilometers north of Hammerfest and was made in 1988. The discovery was production-tested, but the acreage was subsequently relinquished to the authorities. Arne Jacobsen , Assistant Director for Technology and Subsurface, commented: “Several major gas discoveries have been made in the Barents Sea which we still don’t know much about. Norselhøgda is one of a number of discoveries the Norwegian Offshore Directorate believes the companies should take a closer look at.” The Norwegian Offshore Directorate has hired the consulting company Terra Stream Energy to carry out a study that could bring new knowledge about the more precise volume of recoverable resources in the discovery. The reservoir is tight and will probably require stimulation . This is technology that is already being used on the NCS and elsewhere in the world. “The objective is to develop a model that can be shared with the companies so they can make further assessments of mapping and technologies that could help realize a potential development,” added Jacobsen. The study is scheduled to be completed towards the end of this year. In connection with this, the Norwegian Offshore Directorate plans to share the model and hold a professional seminar for the industry. Several comparable discoveries have been made in the area, which include production license 1313 , located to the north of the Norselhøgda discovery and awarded in APA 2025 . The Gro discovery in the Norwegian Sea is another discovery the Norwegian Offshore Directorate hopes to revive, along with the Linerle discovery in the Norwegian Sea. Related Articles Fossil Energy $1.42 trillion at stake as oil & gas production ebbs away: Norway urged to pick up the pace of exploration and tech advancement 3 min read “It’s possible that these discoveries could be viewed in an overall context. There could be benefits to extract if 1313 is developed further. The companies will have an opportunity to apply for Norselhøgda in the next APA round,” noted Jacobsen. The resource potential in the Barents Sea is considered to be considerable, as extensive parts of it remain largely unexplored, with significant acreage that has yet to be opened up for petroleum activity; thus, the development of this potential rests on the development of infrastructure and is particularly relevant for increased gas export opportunities. “Realizing Norselhøgda could be one step towards bringing this all into place,” underlined Jacobsen, while pointing out that the gas proven in the area has a very low CO2 content, just 0.3%, and development and production of gas with such low CO2 content provides added flexibility in exploiting existing infrastructure. articles.title: Shipping equities turn geopolitical risk into an advantage
articles.summary: New research from investment bank Jefferies charts how shipping shares have shifted from being negatively correlated with geopolitical risk during the first decade of this century to moving increasingly in tandem with global instability since 2021. The new report is bullish on tankers, predicting that shares have...
articles.body: Containers Dry Cargo Gas Tankers Shipping equities turn geopolitical risk into an advantage Sam Chambers October 21, 2026 0 598 2 minutes read Photo by Aditya Vyas on Unsplash Photo by Aditya Vyas on Unsplash New research from investment bank Jefferies charts how shipping shares have shifted from being negatively correlated with geopolitical risk during the first decade of this century to moving increasingly in tandem with global instability since 2021. The new report is bullish on tankers, predicting that shares have further room to run, with rates forecast to taper more slowly than the market currently anticipates, in no small part down to the geopolitical correlation. “Since 2021, shipping stocks have also moved with our Geopolitical Risk Index every year, and we expect owners to keep capitalizing on the dislocation into 2027/2028+,” the report predicts. The underlying economics were neatly summarised by Navios Maritime Partners boss Angeliki Frangou during an August earnings call. “The longer ton-mile is like removing from the supply of vessels,” Frangou explained, pointing out that rerouting caused by the Red Sea and Hormuz crises meant ships were spending considerably longer at sea. Jan Rindbo, CEO of Norden, made a similar observation at last month’s Splash Singapore conference. “The world fleet is breaking down into smaller fleets,” Rindbo said, explaining how sanctions, regional conflicts and environmental regulations were fragmenting what was once a relatively unified global merchant fleet. The result is declining fleet efficiency, with more vessels required to transport the same quantities of cargo. Nikolas Tsakos, founder and CEO of Tsakos Energy Navigation, acknowledged the extraordinary opportunities created by the crisis during his company’s September earnings call. “This is uncharted territory, which we are taking advantage of carefully and steadily,” Tsakos said, while stressing his preference for peace even at the expense of today’s record returns. Jefferies believes the tanker rally has further to run, although not necessarily at today’s spectacular spot rates. The bank has lifted its 2027 VLCC earnings forecast from $60,000 to $65,000 a day and its LR2 projection from $30,000 to $34,000, arguing that persistent trading inefficiencies, ageing fleets and future oil inventory rebuilding will support earnings long after the current crisis subsides. It estimates that 51% of crude tankers are at least 15 years old, potentially helping absorb an orderbook equivalent to around 27% of the existing fleet. Not everyone shares that optimism. Norden’s Rindbo has warned that the tanker market could be approaching its peak, prompting the Danish group to reduce tanker exposure and redirect capital towards dry bulk. At Splash Singapore, Christoph Toepfer, CEO of Borealis Maritime, delivered an even starker warning. “The better the party, the worse is the hangover. We’re having a hell of a party right now,” he quipped. The question is how this extraordinary, record-breaking cycle ends. A remarkable chart from Clarksons Research, comparing today’s VLCC boom with previous peaks in capesizes, LNG carriers and container shipping, provides perspective. The current VLCC surge has reached around 17 times its long-term average, dwarfing the peaks recorded in earlier shipping cycles. Yet those previous booms eventually surrendered most of their extraordinary earnings premiums, often within just a few months. The VLCC line on the Clarksons chart ends at today’s extraordinary levels, leaving the subsequent trajectory unanswered. The industry’s history suggests that exceptional earnings eventually correct. What makes this cycle different is that nobody can confidently predict when the geopolitical distortions sustaining it will disappear, or how quickly an apparent shortage of tankers could turn into a surplus.
